diagnosis: HBV calibrated with DDS (about 5000 runs, NSE objective) on 1971-10 to 1997-12, after a one-year warm-up. Initial stores were set close to equilibrium (SM 300 mm, LZ 60 mm). Calibration NSE is 0.903, KGE 0.944, PBIAS -2.2%. On the 1985-1997 sub-period alone, using the same parameters, NSE is 0.908, so performance is steady over time. The parameters fit a permeable fractured-aquifer (limestone) upland catchment: a large FC (~325 mm), LP near 1, BETA ~3.3, a strong PERC (~5 mm/d) feeding a slow groundwater store (K2 ~0.038), a fast quick-flow reservoir above UZL ~55 mm, and short routing (MAXBAS ~2.7). Snow plays a minor role (TT ~0.2, CFMAX ~5.4), and snow parameters such as CWH and CFR are poorly identified, but this hardly matters because only ~4% of precipitation falls as snow. Likely weaknesses: underestimating the highest flood peaks (simulated max 11 vs observed 13.9 mm/d), some error in baseflow recession during dry summers, and timing of snowmelt events. LP at its upper bound suggests ET limitation is weak. I am fairly confident about the volume and recession parameters. UZL, K0 and the snow parameters are less certain. I expect NSE of about 0.85-0.90 in the independent 1998-2008 period.
